title: New Housing Fund Rules: Take What You Can, But Don't Treat It as Savings
dek: The housing provident fund is not savings you can withdraw at will — fraudulent withdrawal gets you pursued for repayment and barred from any withdrawal for three years; but the new rules put renting at the top of the withdrawal list and scrap the rent-to-income ratio cap, so money you should take is still money you should take.
why: Three people in different situations (a self-employed worker, a young professional, a property owner) each run their own numbers, turning the new rules' 20 clause changes into concrete decisions; the second half on flexible-employment contributions and the comparison with the system-inside track is especially informative.
who: Employees who have a provident fund but aren't sure whether to withdraw or leave it; people considering buying a home, converting a commercial loan to a provident fund loan, or contributing as flexible-employment workers; job seekers trying to judge whether a company is well-run.
skip: The opening chit-chat about how the episode came about and the three hosts' positions can be fast-forwarded; start at 13:10 with Zhou Yi's account of actually using it.

points.h: Six months into automatic withdrawal, I paused it myself
points.body: After Zhou Yi turned on Beijing's provident fund rent withdrawal of 2,000 yuan a month with no threshold, she found the money slid into another card the moment it arrived, completely decoupled from the mental account for paying rent; when her spending card ran out at month's end the money was auto-deducted, which only added friction to daily life. After confirming the fund balance earns 1.5% interest, higher than the roughly 0.95% on a one-year bank time deposit, she paused the withdrawal the next day. Yubai noted this contrasts with the advice three years earlier to ‘take everything you can and use everything you can’, and two young colleagues in the department had made the same choice. Lao Qian cautioned that this is indeed a low-efficiency use of funds, but most people can't achieve the efficiency they imagine — people just keep fake books for themselves.

points.h: The provident fund is not savings; not being able to withdraw is the norm
points.body: Yubai walked through an extreme case: a young person loses their job and goes home with no liquid funds, tens of thousands of yuan sitting in the provident fund, but the home is owner-occupied, so it qualifies neither as a home purchase nor as renting; even though the new rules allow withdrawal under the guise of renovation or property fees, if the family has no such needs they are stuck. If they risk it and fabricate a purpose for fraudulent withdrawal, they will be pursued to return the entire withdrawn amount and barred from withdrawing any provident fund for three years. So both ‘take everything you can’ and ‘treat it as forced savings at a rate above demand deposits’ hold up; it depends on the individual.

points.h: The new rules put renting at the top of the withdrawal list
points.body: This revision adjusts 20 clauses in total. First, renovating an owner-occupied home and paying property fees on an owner-occupied home are included as withdrawable purposes for the first time; the provident fund no longer serves only loan-based home purchases. Second, renting withdrawal used to require rent to exceed a set proportion of household wage income; this version removes that limit and puts renting first in the withdrawal scope. Third, flexible-employment workers are formally brought into the system for the first time: self-employed individuals and part-time workers may contribute voluntarily and apply for provident fund loans. In addition, the management center must reply to withdrawal applications within three days and to loan applications within ten days, and nationwide mutual recognition of contribution records is being pushed forward.

points.h: The share of provident fund money lent out fell from 70% to 30%
points.body: The figure Lao Qian saw: this year, the share of provident fund contributions lent out is as low as just over 30%, versus over 70% at the peak — a steady decline in just a few years. In other words, the theoretically most stable, lowest-rate, highest-quality lending channel is actually used by only a bit over 30% of people. That directly reflects how low the willingness to buy homes is. Lao Qian also points out the new rules aim at housing consumption rather than leverage: renting moved to first place, property fees and renovation are withdrawable, thresholds cut sharply — supporting measures as the property market shifts from an incremental to a stock phase, and also echoing the aging trend: the monthly withdrawal ratio turned upward in 2023, exactly matching the retirement of the 1960s cohort.

points.h: If you want to buy a home, be careful about withdrawing
points.body: Yubai warns: provident fund loan limits are tied to account balance — in some cities you can borrow 16 times the balance, in others 20 times, varying by city. Guangzhou also has multiple caps; at application the smallest of several standards applies, for example a minimum 20% down payment for a first or second owner-occupied home means a 1 million yuan home can't be financed above 800,000 yuan; and monthly repayment exceeding 50% of monthly income is also disallowed. So before withdrawing the provident fund as living expenses, check your city's loan rules. Yubai is also cautious about the buy-a-home logic of ‘rent-to-price ratio close to the provident fund rate, only a down payment short’: you still have to consider depreciation, price swings, and how to withstand risk once a 600,000 yuan down payment is locked up.

points.h: Flexible-employment contributors carry the full amount alone
points.body: For flexible-employment workers the contribution base and ratio are calculated the same as for employees, but no employer pays half, so one person bears the full 10% to 24%. The base must be self-declared: below 10,000 yuan no proof is needed; above 10,000 yuan you must log into the individual income tax app and pull tax payment details as documentation, to prevent inflating the base to extract a higher loan limit. Zhou Yi ran the numbers: 10,000 yuan at 10% to 24% is 1,000 to 2,400 yuan, and this money is not counted toward individual income tax, but it's a loss if you never use it. Also, most pilot cities require 6 to 12 consecutive months of contributions before you can apply for a provident fund loan, and most do not allow one-time back payments.

points.h: Inside the system, the provident fund is invisible welfare
points.body: Zhou Yi asked a friend with a public-institution post back home, who openly showed a screenshot of the provident fund account: the monthly deposit is more than twice hers, and the balance already exceeds her savings; the friend lives at home with no rental need, so the provident fund just accumulates as forced savings or future loan capacity, plus there is an occupational annuity, and the contribution base counts bonuses and subsidies in full. Lao Qian adds: the provident fund is tax-free, and with individual pension contributions capped at 12,000 yuan a year and taxed at 3% on withdrawal, being inside the system already carries an extra layer of tax advantage. On the data: in 2025 the national average annual wage for urban non-private unit employees was 129,441 yuan, versus 71,590 yuan for private units — while working hours run the other way.

points.h: Full provident fund contributions are a slice for judging a company
points.body: Lao Qian's judgment on ‘is a company that pays the provident fund a more ideal choice’ has not changed at all: a company that pays the provident fund in full respects its employees and respects the rules, which means it is probably well-run in every respect, and won't play cat-and-mouse with policy. He goes further: this points to not making profit maximization the first goal, to treating people as people, and the invisible returns show up elsewhere. Zhou Yi ran the numbers: on a wage base of 100, take-home is just over 70, but the boss pays over 130, and everyone along the chain feels wronged. Lao Qian cites Ford's Model T wage increase — letting workers afford a car and have time to use it wasn't capitalist conscience, it was simply a better utility function.

quotes.text: It arrived, but because your phone gets so many app notifications you don't look carefully — say it reminds you 2,000 yuan came in, and then it just sits in that card until the end of the month, when my spending card is used up and it gets auto-deducted from that card.
But the fact is people keep fake books for themselves, people withdraw on impulse for all sorts of reasons, people are very good at self-deception.
You really can't treat the provident fund as a deposit, because your bank deposit you can withdraw at any time, but the provident fund you can't.
And it's the highest-quality lending channel, the rate is so low, yet only a bit over 30% of people took out loans — what was the ratio at the peak before? Over 70% — in just a few short years.
I think a company that pays the provident fund in full shows it respects its employees and respects the rules.

Treating people as people doesn't mean raising costs; it also means one person's spending, the household sector's spending, becomes the corporate sector's income, and the corporate sector's spending becomes the household sector's wages — the two form a virtuous cycle.
Take everything you can and use everything you can — buying a home, building, renovating, repaying a loan, renting, retirement, leaving the country — all of it can be used.
